title: Canonical differential presheaf sequence on polynomial pairs
statement:
Let $A\to B\to C$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings. Use a common infinite size bound and small skeletons [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal C_{T/S}$ be the opposite category of augmented polynomial $S$-algebras $P\to T$, and let $\mathcal E$ be the opposite category of pairs $U=(P\to B,Q\to C)$ with $P$ polynomial over $A$, $Q$ polynomial over $P$, and compatible augmentations; morphisms before opposites are compatible algebra maps preserving the augmentations. Give these categories the identity-cover topology. Define $u_1(U)=P\to B$, $u_2(U)=Q\to C$, $u_3(U)=Q\otimes_P B\to C$ and $g_i^{-1}$ by precomposition, with structural rings and augmentations as in [lem-trf-cotangent-lower-shriek]. Write $F_{T/S}(P\to T)=\Omega_{P/S}\otimes_P T$ with its differential restriction maps [lem-trf-cotangent-sheaf-model, def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and form the constant-$C$ module presheaves
$$M_1=g_1^{-1}F_{B/A}\otimes_{\underline B}\underline C,\qquad M_2=g_2^{-1}F_{C/A},\qquad M_3=g_3^{-1}F_{C/B}$$
using [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. There is a canonical short exact sequence $0\to M_1\xrightarrow{a}M_2\xrightarrow{b}M_3\to0$. Its values at $U$ identify canonically with
$$0\to\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_P C\xrightarrow{a_U}\Omega_{Q/A}\otimes_Q C\xrightarrow{b_U}\Omega_{Q/P}\otimes_Q C\to0.$$
Here the third identification is $\Omega_{Q\otimes_P B/B}\otimes_{Q\otimes_P B}C\simeq\Omega_{Q/P}\otimes_Q C$, taking $\mathrm d(q\otimes1)\otimes c$ to $\mathrm dq\otimes c$; $a_U$ takes $\mathrm dp\otimes c$ to $\mathrm dp\otimes c$, and $b_U$ takes $\mathrm dq\otimes c$ to its relative differential. These two maps commute with every restriction map. For any polynomial coordinates $P=A[x_s]$, $Q=P[y_t]$, the displayed sequence is the inclusion and projection sequence $0\to\bigoplus_s C\,\mathrm dx_s\to(\bigoplus_s C\,\mathrm dx_s)\oplus(\bigoplus_t C\,\mathrm dy_t)\to\bigoplus_t C\,\mathrm dy_t\to0$. No naturality of the coordinate splitting and no flatness of $C$ over $Q$ are asserted or required.

proof.text: Obtain a bar system from lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar and the projection record from lem-trf-cotangent-lower-shriek. Construct the coefficient presheaf on the full presentation site by the universal property of Kahler differentials followed by scalar extension: a presentation map sends c tensor dx to c tensor d(h(x)). Equality on these generators proves the functor identities. The first evaluation identification is the composite of the ring-isomorphism transport and extension-of-scalars transitivity, sending c tensor (b tensor dp) to c g(b) tensor dp. The second is induced by the second projection ring isomorphism. These are actual module isomorphisms with the stated generator formulas.

source.place: Tag 08QU (lemma-triangle-ses), proof, evaluation at a polynomial pair and assembly of the sequence.

proof.text: Apply differential base change with $R=P$, $R'=B$, $S=Q$, interchanging the tensor factors $B\otimes_P Q\simeq Q\otimes_P B=D$ by $b\otimes q\mapsto q\otimes b$. It gives $\Omega_{D/B}\simeq D\otimes_Q\Omega_{Q/P}$, taking $\mathrm d(q\otimes1)$ to $1\otimes\mathrm d_{Q/P}q$. Tensor with $C$ via the given augmentation $D\to C$ and cancel $D$ by $(d\otimes\eta)\otimes c\mapsto\eta\otimes d c$, inverse $\eta\otimes c\mapsto(1\otimes\eta)\otimes c$. Thus $M_3(U)\simeq\Omega_{Q/P}\otimes_Q C$ with precisely the stated generator formula. For a pair map $(\phi:P\to P',\psi:Q\to Q')$, the induced $D\to D'$ sends $q\otimes b$ to $\psi(q)\otimes b$; both routes on $\mathrm d(q\otimes1)\otimes c$ give $\mathrm d_{Q'/P'}\psi(q)\otimes c$. These elements generate, proving naturality of this identification.

source.place: Tag 00RV (lemma-differentials-base-change), statement and generator formula in the proof; used in Tag 08QU.

proof.text: The $A$-derivation $p\mapsto\mathrm d_{Q/A}p$ and the $A$-derivation $q\mapsto\mathrm d_{Q/P}q$ induce maps of differential modules by the defining universal property; extending scalars gives $a_U$ and $b_U$. The second derivation kills $P$, so $b_Ua_U=0$. For a pair map $(\phi,\psi)$ before opposites, restrictions send $\mathrm dp\otimes c$ to $\mathrm d\phi(p)\otimes c$ and $\mathrm dq\otimes c$ to $\mathrm d\psi(q)\otimes c$. The $a$ square commutes because $\psi(p)=\phi(p)$ inside $Q'$; the $b$ square commutes because both routes send $\mathrm d_{Q/A}q\otimes c$ to $\mathrm d_{Q'/P'}\psi(q)\otimes c$. Universal differentials generate their modules, so these checks prove equality on all elements. With step 2 they define $C$-linear presheaf morphisms $a:M_1\to M_2$ and $b:M_2\to M_3$, canonically and independently of coordinates.

source.place: Tag 08QU (lemma-triangle-ses), proof, evaluation at a polynomial pair and assembly of the sequence.

proof.text: Choose polynomial coordinates $P=A[x_s]$, $Q=P[y_t]=A[x_s,y_t]$; the last identification is substitution of finite polynomials, with inverse fixing $A,x_s,y_t$. Apply the arbitrary-variable differential-basis lemma to $P/A$, $Q/A$ and $Q/P$, and its scalar-extension clause with algebra $C$. The bases are respectively $(\mathrm dx_s)$, $(\mathrm dx_s,\mathrm dy_t)$ and $(\mathrm dy_t)$. Step 3 sends $\mathrm dx_s$ to $\mathrm dx_s$, and sends $(\mathrm dx_s,\mathrm dy_t)$ to $(0,\mathrm dy_t)$, since the relative derivation kills $P$. Thus the maps are $v\mapsto(v,0)$ and $(v,w)\mapsto w$ on the displayed direct sums. They are respectively injective and surjective, and the kernel of the projection consists exactly of $(v,0)$. This proves all objectwise short exactness and coordinate-form assertions. Every sum has finite support even for infinite variable sets. No tensor-preservation-of-injections or flatness assumption is used.

source.place: Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), basis calculation, extended to arbitrary variable sets as in the cited node; implements the split polynomial sequence in Tag 08QU.

proof.text: For each pair, choose its polynomial coordinates and apply step 4. Transport its short exact module sequence through the three evaluation isomorphisms. Objectwise monomorphisms and epimorphisms give the corresponding presheaf monomorphism and epimorphism. To prove middle exactness, lift every presheaf map killed by b through the objectwise kernel a. Uniqueness of the lift, checked after composing with the monomorphism a, proves its naturality. This is the kernel universal property in the functor category, hence the presheaf short complex is exact and short exact. No passage through a chain complex or free-nerve evaluation lemma is needed.
